problem: Existing RGB-D datasets have too few images, limited scene coverage (single rooms, single floors, or a few office buildings), limited or blurry viewpoints from hand-held video, synthetic imagery, or poor global camera alignment. None offers high-quality RGB-D panoramas densely covering entire real homes.
motivation: Data-driven scene understanding, and later embodied navigation, depends on the quantity and quality of real indoor data. Tripod-based Matterport capture gives motion-blur-free HDR color and depth, globally registered 360° panoramas about 2.25 m apart across whole buildings. The authors argue this enables new supervised and self-supervised tasks, e.g. wide-baseline correspondences, loop closures, clean normals, and whole-building context.
key_idea: Release a building-scale real RGB-D dataset with precisely registered panoramas, textured meshes, and 3D region and object instance annotations. Demonstrate its value by training baselines on five scene-understanding tasks that exploit these properties.
insight: Precise global registration plus dense, diverse viewpoint sampling is what makes the data useful. It yields wide-baseline supervision that transfers. Pretraining a ResNet-50 descriptor on Matterport3D before SUN3D lowers keypoint error at 95% recall from 10.5% (SUN3D only) to 9.2% (Table 1). Adding Matterport3D to view-overlap training raises SUN3D nDCG from 83.34 to 85.45 (Table 2). Clean depth-derived normals generalize across datasets while noisy ones do not: the MP-trained normal model stays reasonable on NYUv2 (mean 26.34°), but the NYUv2-trained model degrades badly on MP (33.91°) (Table 4). Panoramic field of view improves room-type classification for most categories (Table 5). For navigation research, the lasting contribution is the 90 whole-building scenes and the panorama viewpoint graph, which later underpin the Matterport3D Simulator (R2R), Habitat MP3D ObjectNav/PointNav, and related benchmarks.
method: Data acquisition: tripod-mounted Matterport rig with 3 RGB and 3 depth cameras rotating to 6 orientations, giving 18 HDR RGB-D images (1280x1024) per panorama at human eye height. Panoramas are spaced about 2.25 m ± 0.57 m across the whole walkable floor plan.

Reconstruction/registration: images are stitched into skyboxes, 6-DoF poses come from global bundle adjustment (estimated average registration error ≤1 cm), and a single textured mesh is built per building (Poisson / voxel-hashing reconstructions provided). Totals: 90 buildings, 10,800 panoramas, 194,400 RGB-D images.

Semantic annotation: annotators draw 2D floor-plan polygons per room-like region, which are snapped to walls/floor and extruded to the ceiling, with categories such as bedroom or hallway. Objects are then 'painted' per region mesh with the ScanNet crowdsourcing interface (AMT, verified by 10 experts), giving 50,811 object instances. 1,659 raw labels are mapped to 40 WordNet-based categories.

Benchmark tasks with a 61/11/18 train/val/test scene split: (1) keypoint descriptor learning with a ResNet-50 triplet Siamese network (512-d, L2 hinge loss) on wide-baseline SIFT correspondences; (2) view-overlap / loop-closure retrieval with a ResNet-50 triplet network plus overlap-ratio regression loss.

(3) Surface normal estimation from RGB with Zhang et al.'s VGG-16 encoder-decoder, pretrained on SUNCG then MP and/or NYUv2. (4) Region-type classification over 12 room categories with ResNet-50 on single images vs panoramas. (5) Semantic voxel labeling with a ScanNet-style 3D CNN on 1.5×1.5×3 m subvolumes at 2 cm voxels over 20 classes.

setting.backbone: Task-specific baselines trained from scratch/pretrained: ResNet-50 (keypoint descriptor, view overlap, region classification), VGG-16-based encoder-decoder of Zhang et al. (surface normals), ScanNet-style 3D CNN (semantic voxel labeling)
setting.training_data: Matterport3D 61 training scenes. Plus 17 SUN3D scenes for keypoint/overlap, SUNCG synthetic pretraining and NYUv2 fine-tuning for normals, and 52,355 voxel subvolumes (418,840 with rotation augmentation) for voxel labeling.
setting.observation: RGB-D images / RGB-D panoramas (HDR color + depth), 3D voxelized meshes for voxel labeling
setting.action_space: N/A (dataset paper; no embodied agent or actions)
setting.simulator: none (static dataset; later the basis of the Matterport3D Simulator and Habitat MP3D scenes)

results:
Matterport3D provides 90 buildings, 10,800 panoramas, 194,400 RGB-D images, 46,561 m² floor space and 50,811 annotated object instances, larger than ScanNet or 2D-3D-S. Pretraining on it improves every tested task:
- Keypoint matching error on SUN3D drops to 9.2% at 95% recall, vs 37.8% for SIFT and 10.5% for SUN3D-only training.
- View-overlap nDCG on SUN3D rises to 85.45 from 83.34.
- NYUv2 normal estimation reaches 20.89° mean error, beating the SUNCG→NYUv2 state of the art at 22.07°.
- Semantic voxel labeling reaches 70.3% accuracy.
limitations: No ground-truth camera poses, so registration accuracy (≤1 cm average, occasional ≥10 cm misalignments) is only subjectively estimated.

Static, sparsely sampled panoramic viewpoints (~2.25 m apart) rather than continuous trajectories. The paper itself defines no embodied/navigation task; that requires later simulators (Matterport3D Simulator, Habitat).
Baselines are simple adaptations of existing models. Some categories have very low voxel-labeling accuracy (e.g. sofa, bed, toilet), and the scale is only 90 scenes (61 for training).
